title: TKA Bahasa Inggris - Narrative Text
subtitle: Latihan Mandiri 15 Soal
difficulty_summary: 20% Mudah | 60% Sedang | 20% Sulit. Kerjakan dengan jujur dan teliti.

passages.title: Mouse Deer and the King's Belt
text: One hot afternoon, Mouse Deer was walking through the forest when he suddenly saw Tiger in front of him. Tiger had not eaten for two days, and his eyes shone when he saw the little animal.

"Today is my lucky day," said Tiger. "You will be my lunch." Mouse Deer was frightened, but he knew that running away was useless. Tiger was much faster than he was. Then he noticed a large python sleeping in a circle under a tree nearby. He had an idea.

"I'm sorry, Tiger," said Mouse Deer calmly, "but I cannot be your lunch. The King has ordered me to guard his belt." He pointed at the sleeping python. "It is the most beautiful belt in the world. Only the King is allowed to wear it."

Tiger looked at the snake. Its skin was shining in the sun. "I want to wear the King's belt," he said. "Let me try it on!" Mouse Deer pretended to think for a long time. "Well," he said at last, "you may try it, but first let me go far away so the King will not blame me."

Tiger agreed. Mouse Deer ran as fast as he could. When he was far enough, he shouted, "Now, Tiger! Put on the belt!" Tiger wrapped the python around his waist. The snake woke up and squeezed him tightly. Tiger roared and struggled for a long time before he finally escaped. By then, Mouse Deer was safe at home, and Tiger had learned not to trust Mouse Deer again.

passages.title: The Golden Snail
text: Long ago, in a kingdom in East Java, there lived a kind princess named Candra Kirana. She was engaged to Prince Raden Inu Kertapati, and the two loved each other very much. However, her half-sister, Dewi Galuh, was jealous because she also wanted to marry the prince.
Dewi Galuh asked an evil witch to help her. The witch cast a spell on Candra Kirana and turned her into a golden snail. Then she threw the snail into a river, far away from the palace.

One day, an old woman named Mbok Rondo was fishing in the river. Instead of fish, she found a beautiful golden snail in her net. She took it home and put it in a clay jar. The next morning, when she came back from the market, she was surprised to find delicious food on her table and her small house clean and tidy. The same thing happened every day.

Curious, Mbok Rondo pretended to go to the market one morning but hid behind the door instead. To her surprise, she saw the snail come out of the jar and change into a beautiful young woman, who began to cook and sweep the floor. Mbok Rondo quickly broke the shell, and the princess could not turn back into a snail. Candra Kirana told her the whole story.

Meanwhile, Prince Raden Inu Kertapati had been searching for his lost bride for months. One day, he arrived at Mbok Rondo's village and recognized the princess at once. The spell was broken, and they returned to the palace together. Dewi Galuh was punished for her evil plan, and Candra Kirana invited Mbok Rondo to live with her in the palace.

passages.title: The Wallet on the Bus
text: Raka was on his way home from his part-time job at a printing shop when he saw a brown wallet on the empty seat beside him. The bus was almost empty, and the woman who had been sitting there had just got off at the market.

He opened the wallet. Inside there were an identity card, a photo of two small children, and seven hundred thousand rupiah. Raka took a deep breath. He had been saving for weeks to buy a new phone, and the money in the wallet was exactly what he still needed.

For a moment, he thought nobody would ever know. Then he looked again at the photo of the children and imagined the woman searching for her wallet, maybe with no money to buy food for them. He closed the wallet and put it in his bag.

Instead of going home, Raka got off at the next stop and walked back to the market. He asked a parking attendant if he had seen a woman in a green headscarf. The man pointed to a small shop where a woman was crying and talking to the shop owner. When Raka gave her the wallet, she cried even more, but this time with joy. The money, she said, was for her son's school fees.

She tried to give him some of the money as a reward, but Raka refused politely. As he walked to the bus stop again, he felt lighter than he had felt for weeks. He still did not have a new phone, but he knew he had made the right choice.

questions.question: Why did Tiger want to eat Mouse Deer?

options.B: Mouse Deer had stolen his food.
options.C: The King had ordered him to do it.
options.D: He had not eaten for two days.

questions.explanation: Paragraf 1: Tiger had not eaten for two days.

questions.question: What is the King's belt in the story actually?

options.A: A golden belt owned by the King

questions.explanation: Mouse Deer menunjuk ular piton yang tidur melingkar dan menyebutnya ikat pinggang raja. Itu tipuannya.

questions.question: Which part of the story is the complication?

options.A: Mouse Deer is walking through the forest on a hot afternoon.
options.B: Tiger learns not to trust Mouse Deer again.
options.D: Tiger finds Mouse Deer and wants to eat him.

questions.explanation: Komplikasi adalah munculnya masalah bagi tokoh utama: Tiger ingin memangsa Mouse Deer. Pilihan pertama adalah orientasi; dua pilihan lain bagian resolusi dan koda.

questions.question:
Which words best describe Mouse Deer in the story?
(1) Clever
(2) Calm under pressure
(3) Greedy
(4) Honest
questions.explanation: Mouse Deer menemukan ide menipu Tiger (cerdik) dan berbicara calmly walaupun takut (tenang). Ia tidak serakah, dan karena menipu, ia tidak bisa disebut jujur.

questions.question: What would most likely happen if Tiger met Mouse Deer again?

options.A: Tiger would not believe what Mouse Deer said.
options.B: Tiger would ask Mouse Deer for another belt.
options.C: Tiger would thank Mouse Deer for the lesson.
options.D: Tiger would invite Mouse Deer to meet the King.

questions.explanation: Memprediksi kelanjutan cerita: kalimat terakhir menyebut Tiger had learned not to trust Mouse Deer again, sehingga Tiger tidak akan memercayai ucapan Mouse Deer.

questions.question: Why did Dewi Galuh ask the witch for help?

options.A: She wanted to marry the prince herself.
options.B: She wanted to become the queen of the kingdom.
options.C: She wanted to find her lost sister.
options.D: She wanted to punish Mbok Rondo.

questions.explanation: Dewi Galuh cemburu because she also wanted to marry the prince.

questions.question: How did Mbok Rondo discover the secret of the golden snail?

options.A: The prince told her about the spell.
options.B: The snail spoke to her at the market.
options.C: She hid and watched the snail change into a woman.
options.D: Her neighbours saw the princess cooking.

questions.explanation: Mbok Rondo berpura-pura ke pasar lalu bersembunyi di balik pintu dan melihat keong berubah menjadi gadis.

questions.question: Why could Candra Kirana not turn back into a snail?

options.C: Mbok Rondo had broken the shell.
options.D: She had left the clay jar.

questions.explanation: Hubungan sebab-akibat: Mbok Rondo quickly broke the shell, and the princess could not turn back into a snail.

questions.question: Which statement shows that the story is a fantasy, not a real event?

options.A: A princess was engaged to a prince.
options.B: An old woman went fishing in a river.
options.C: A witch turned a princess into a golden snail.
options.D: A prince searched for his bride for months.

questions.explanation: Menilai realitas atau fantasi: manusia berubah menjadi keong karena mantra tidak mungkin terjadi di dunia nyata. Tiga peristiwa lain masih mungkin terjadi.

questions.question: What is the moral value of the story?

options.A: Jealousy and evil plans will finally bring punishment.
options.B: We should never go fishing alone.
options.C: Old people should live in a palace.

questions.explanation: Pesan moral tersirat: rencana jahat Dewi Galuh karena iri akhirnya terbongkar dan ia dihukum, sedangkan kebaikan Mbok Rondo dibalas.

questions.question: Where did Raka find the wallet?

options.B: On the bus seat next to him
options.C: In front of a shop at the market

questions.explanation: he saw a brown wallet on the empty seat beside him, di dalam bus.

questions.question: What made Raka decide to return the wallet?

options.A: He was afraid the police would find out.
options.B: He imagined the owner and her children needing the money.
options.C: The parking attendant told him to return it.
options.D: He already had enough money for a new phone.

questions.explanation: Paragraf 3: ia melihat lagi foto anak-anak itu dan membayangkan pemiliknya mungkin tidak bisa membeli makanan untuk mereka.

questions.question: The phrase he felt lighter in the last paragraph suggests that Raka felt ....

options.B: relieved and happy with his decision
options.C: hungry because he had not eaten

questions.explanation: Makna kiasan: felt lighter berarti hatinya lega, tidak terbebani, karena ia tahu sudah memilih dengan benar.

questions.question:
Which parts of the story best show Raka's honesty?
(1) He closed the wallet and put it in his bag.
(2) He got off at the next stop and walked back to the market.
(3) He had been saving for weeks to buy a new phone.
(4) He refused the reward politely.
questions.explanation: Kembali ke pasar untuk mencari pemilik dan menolak imbalan menunjukkan kejujuran dan ketulusannya. Menyimpan dompet di tas belum menunjukkan niatnya, dan menabung untuk ponsel adalah latar cerita.

questions.question: How is The Wallet on the Bus different from The Golden Snail?

options.A: It has no problem for the main character to solve.
options.B: It tells a realistic event without magic.
options.C: It does not have a moral message.
options.D: It is told by the main character himself.

questions.explanation: Membandingkan dua teks: The Wallet on the Bus realistis, tanpa unsur gaib, sedangkan The Golden Snail memuat sihir. Keduanya punya masalah dan pesan moral, dan keduanya dikisahkan dengan sudut pandang orang ketiga.
